question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g=1-4x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot (-4) \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$
